verdict.rationale: GrowthBook documents a full REST API with a toggle endpoint and an official MCP server that makes authenticated REST calls with agent guardrails, and a runtime probe confirmed creating a flag through the API. For governance, it documents draft revisions with required approval before publishing, and its API docs state that risky changes are held until a person confirms them. Missing for 10: only a single thin line ties approval enforcement to API/agent-originated writes, approval workflows are gated to the top pricing tier, there is no CLI evidence, and there is no independent hands-on corroboration of agent changes being routed through review.

support.subject: As an AI agent, I can create and toggle flags through documented APIs, CLIs, or MCP — and the platform can force my changes through approval workflows instead of letting me write to production unreviewed

citations.quote: GrowthBook offers a full REST API for interacting with the application.
automate it (for example, from a deploy script) with the toggle feature endpoint, which switches a flag on or off in one or more environments.
The official GrowthBook MCP server is a thin bridge: it loads GrowthBook Agent Skills (workflows and guardrails) and makes authenticated calls to the GrowthBook REST API.
Draft feature revisions, request review, resolve merge conflicts, and require approval before publishing.
Require confirmation holds risky changes until a person confirms them in GrowthBook.
